stories.headline: US Central Command Strikes Iranian Targets as Conflict Escalates and Casualty Reports Grow
stories.body:
US Central Command launched attacks targeting Iranian air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, and mine laying capabilities. The United States unveiled measures on August 19 to tighten its financial siege around Iran's ports. The measures also tightened the blockade around Iranian ports. Jordan reported detecting 13 ballistic missiles in its airspace. Jordan intercepted 10 of those missiles. Mojtaba Khamenei appointed Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps founder Mohsen Rezaee as his representative on Iran's Supreme National Security Council.

US Vice President JD Vance declined to offer a timeline for the end of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Vance said that he would not call it a war. He said there is no active shooting right now. Vance said major combat operations against Iran lasted about six weeks. Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna called Vance's statements unbelievable gaslighting. Vance said a deal transferring control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves to the US would help lower global oil costs. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas flowed through the Strait of Hormuz before the war.

Reports differ on casualties from strikes during the conflict. An air strike on an Iranian elementary school in Minab killed more than 150 people on the first day of the war. A February 28 US air attack in Minab killed at least 156 people. Most of those killed in that attack were schoolchildren. Reports also differ about an attack on a wedding. An attack on a wedding party in Sirik reportedly killed at least five people. That attack injured nearly 70 others. The Iranian Red Crescent reported that four people were killed when missile shrapnel struck a home during a wedding in Kuhestak. The Red Crescent said more than 50 people were wounded in that strike. Vance said sometimes things happen when asked if an American strike was responsible for deaths at an Iranian wedding.

Casualties have also mounted among American troops. As of August, 18 US service members have been killed in the conflict with Iran. A total of 750 US service members have been wounded.

Questions have arisen regarding American weapon supplies. US President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US has virtually unlimited amounts of mid- to high-grade munitions. Trump called reports of dwindling US ammunition supplies 100% wrong. He described those spreading such reports as treasonous. But Reuters reported on August 4 that the US military has used virtually all of its ATACMS and PrSM surface-to-surface missile stockpiles during the war with Iran. Military leaders warned Trump in recent weeks that US supplies of Patriot missile interceptors were falling.

stories.headline: Rescuers Search Hydro Tunnels in Nepal After Devastating Himalayan Flash Floods
stories.body:
Rescuers used rafts and drones to search for survivors trapped inside hydro tunnels along Nepal's Trishuli River. A glacial collapse in the Himalayas triggered flash flooding and debris flows across the Nepal-Tibet border.

More than 1,200 people have been confirmed dead after the Nepal-Tibet floods. Over 5,500 people remain missing. Nepal flood victims are set to be identified through DNA testing. Two additional Australians were confirmed safe, reducing the number of missing Australians to 36.

Helicopters airlifted more than 4,000 people across Rasuwa and Nuwakot after the August 26 Bhote Koshi-Trishuli flood in Nepal. Captain Bimal Sharma of Simrik Air said flood rescue missions in the Trishuli gorge were tougher than Everest-season flying. He said this was due to missing landing spots and inaccurate coordinates.

Unicef warned that at least 22,000 children in Nepal urgently need safe drinking water and better sanitation.

stories.headline: US Energy Firms Sign Multi-Billion Dollar Deals for Venezuelan Oil Assets
stories.body:
US energy companies signed multi-billion-dollar deals with Venezuela after control of key oil assets went to the US. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright traveled to Venezuela to oversee agreement signings with Chevron, GE Vernova, and ENI. Chevron made a $7 billion bet on Venezuela's oil industry.

The US-Venezuela agreement grants the United States access to more than 65 billion barrels of oil in Venezuela. Venezuela possesses the world's largest proven crude oil reserves, estimated at 303 billion barrels. Interim leader Delcy Rodríguez estimated Venezuela will make $209 billion in profit from the energy deals over 25 years. Rodríguez assumed power as interim president in January after former president Nicolás Maduro was abducted by US special forces.

Critics have described the multi-billion-dollar US oil agreement in Venezuela as modern-day colonialism. Venezuelan opposition figure María Corina Machado called for a democratic transition after the US-Venezuela oil deal. Machado said that the wealth of our subsoil does not belong to an illegitimate regime, but belongs to the Venezuelan people.

stories.headline: UN and WMO Warn of Unprecedented Threats from Supersized El Niño Event
stories.body:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres said that El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The World Meteorological Organization warned that the current El Niño could be the strongest recorded since records began four decades ago. The disappearance of anchovies along the South American Pacific coast is signaling a major El Niño event.

Ocean temperatures at the center of El Niño measured 2.6 degrees Celsius above the 30-year average. Models forecast a peak of 4 degrees Celsius in November. UK Met Office projections indicate equatorial Pacific ocean temperatures could spike by 3 degrees Celsius when El Niño peaks in late 2026 or early 2027.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said the agency has launched its largest mobilization in its 50-year history to save lives. The World Food Programme estimated that El Niño is likely to push about 50 million people into acute hunger. The British government is planning a public campaign advising citizens to stock up on tinned food and water for national emergencies.

In Indonesia, Professor Bambang Hero Saharjo said research indicates this year's El Niño could cause wildfires to burn up to 11 million hectares. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded over 50,000 cases of respiratory infections linked to wildfires between July and August. That figure included more than 12,000 cases in children under five.

stories.headline: Palestinian Teenagers Killed in West Bank Clash as Demolitions and Gaza Attacks Continue
stories.body:
Israeli forces and settlers shot dead 16-year-old Khalil Abu Alia and 19-year-old Omar al-Nassan in al-Mughayyir. The UN recorded that at least 81 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year. Israeli police arrested a 19-year-old settler on suspicion of involvement in an attack on the West Bank village of Qusra.

In Khirbet al-Taban, Israeli troops demolished homes belonging to 12 Palestinian families, leaving 70 residents homeless. Human rights group B'Tselem said Khirbet al-Taban is the 66th Palestinian community wiped off the map since October 2023.

In Gaza, an Israeli drone strike in Gaza City's Rimal neighborhood killed one person and injured several others. The Gaza Health Ministry reports that at least 73,470 people have been killed in Gaza since October 2023. That figure includes over 1,330 people killed since the October ceasefire. Israeli officials gave differing estimates of control in Gaza. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel controls 60% of Gaza and will not withdraw. Israel's Deputy Chief of General Staff Maj Gen Tamir Yadai said Israel controls 65% of the Gaza Strip. Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir presented a plan aiming to remove roughly two million Palestinians from the Gaza Strip over seven years.

stories.headline: ISRO Successfully Launches EOS-05 Earth Observation Satellite into Orbit
stories.body:
The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully launched the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite on September 4. The satellite was launched aboard a Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle rocket. The GSLV-F17 rocket lifted off following a 27.5-hour countdown from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. Lift off took place at 2.55 a.m. on September 4. The GSLV placed EOS-05 into a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit 18 minutes after lifting off.

EOS-05 is India's first imaging satellite designed to monitor Earth from a geosynchronous orbit approximately 36,000 km high. The EOS-05 satellite is also designated as Gisat-1A. EOS-05 carries two multispectral imagers. One of these imagers features a spatial resolution of 42 metres per pixel. ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said that EOS-05 is the heaviest satellite ever launched by a GSLV rocket. The satellite weighs 2,367 kg.

The rocket carrying the satellite had specific physical dimensions. The GSLV-F17 rocket stands 51.7 metres tall. It has a liftoff mass of 420.5 tonnes.

This successful launch replaces an earlier failed attempt. EOS-05 replaces the EOS-03 mission. The EOS-03 mission failed in August 2021 due to a cryogenic upper stage ignition anomaly. Prior to this launch, ISRO had experienced another setback. ISRO had not conducted any launch missions since the failure of the PSLV-C62 mission on January 12, 2026.

The new satellite adds to India's existing capabilities in space. India had 21 operational Earth observation satellites as of February 2026. ISRO plans to expand its space operations further this year. Narayanan announced that ISRO plans six more launches in the current financial year. These future missions include the navigation satellite NVS-03. They also include the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission.

stories.headline: Indian Foreign Minister Jaishankar Visits Kyiv and Reaffirms Stance on Peace and Energy
stories.body:
Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv. Jaishankar invited Sybiha to visit India. Jaishankar also met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during his visit to Kyiv.

Jaishankar said in Kyiv that India is ready to extend any help in any manner to end the Russia-Ukraine war. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek that endless war must give way to the end of war. Jaishankar rejected Western claims that buying Russian oil bankrolls the war. He said India's energy sourcing is based on securing supplies for its 1.4 billion people.

The visit took place during ongoing military attacks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched jet-powered Shahed drones over Kyiv during Jaishankar's visit. Zelenskyy said the Shahed drones were built with assistance from Iran. An Indian national was killed in an attack in Kyiv two days before Jaishankar's visit. Russian attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea have caused the deaths of five Indian seafarers.

stories.headline: Political Debate Erupts in India Over Revised GDP Growth Calculation Method
stories.body:
India revised its GDP calculation base year from 2011-12 to 2022-23 in February 2026. BJP chief spokesperson Anil Baluni said India has revised its GDP base year nine times since Independence.

A political argument erupted over official economic figures. The Bharatiya Janata Party accused the Congress party of using flawed calculations to convert India's 7.8% GDP growth figure into an imaginary 2.6%. Former Indian finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg argued that first-quarter GDP growth would be 2.6% in nominal terms without the downward revision of the previous year's base figure. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh claimed that GDP estimates across four years since 2022-23 were revised downwards by a total of 43 lakh crore rupees.

Government officials and economists defended the numbers. Sanjeev Sanyal, a member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council, denied allegations of GDP data manipulation. World Bank executive director Neelkanth Mishra defended India's 7.8% first-quarter GDP growth figure, dismissing claims of data manipulation as egregiously wrong. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation reported that India's manufacturing sector grew 9.2% in the April-June quarter of FY 2026-27. Credit rating agency JCR upgraded India's sovereign rating from 'BBB+' to 'A-' with a stable outlook. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju shared a video of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang praising India's IT growth and AI focus amid the controversy.
